original.target_description: Main effect of brand name on the Attribute Perception Index. Original Study 1 undergraduates; ANCOVA with involvement covariate.

n.sample_role: 126 recruited undergraduates; analytic n for target ANCOVA not explicitly stated
n.exclusions: No target-specific exclusions or complete-case count established.
n.quote: One hundred and twenty-six undergraduate students in a large northeastern university participated in the study for partial course credit.

es.quote: addition, the main effect of brand name was significant (F(1,117) = 9.51, p < .01).

p.quote: addition, the main effect of brand name was significant (F(1,117) = 9.51, p < .01).

replication.target_description: Main effect of brand name on the Attribute Perception Index. Japanese online adult sample; full-sample ANOVA.

n.sample_role: Japanese online participants included in final analysis
n.exclusions: 247 excluded for failing instructional manipulation check and attention check question; paper recruitment statement says 1000, inconsistent with 823 + 247.
n.quote: Finally, the data of 823 participants (mean age = 40.77, SD of age = 10.48, 428 males, 391 females, 4 did not prefer to say) were analyzed.

es.quote: main effect of sound symbolism of brand name ( F 1,821 = 7.492, p = 0.006, η 2 p = 0.009) such that frosh (vs. frish) had higher ratings in the attribute perception index. However, the results of the analysis did not show a three-way interaction ( F 1,821 = 1.053, p = 0.305, η 2 p = 0.001) or an interaction between sound symbolism and diagnosticity ( F 1,821 = 0.118, p = 0.731, η 2 p = 0.000).

p.quote: main effect of sound symbolism of brand name ( F 1,821 = 7.492, p = 0.006, η 2 p = 0.009) such that frosh (vs. frish) had higher ratings in the attribute perception index. However, the results of the analysis did not show a three-way interaction ( F 1,821 = 1.053, p = 0.305, η 2 p = 0.001) or an interaction between sound symbolism and diagnosticity ( F 1,821 = 0.118, p = 0.731, η 2 p = 0.000).

reported_success.location: Discussion, Which findings can or cannot be replicated?
reported_success.quote: Our replication attempts successfully replicated two findings (Klink, 2000 ; Shrum et al., 2012 ) and partially replicated one of them (Yorkston and Menon, 2004 ).

notes: Reported success is the authors’ study-level verdict.  Original is an authors’ manuscript with different pagination. It reports ANCOVA, whereas replication reports ANOVA. Analytic n is not separately printed.
